accords.name: Peach
accords.inspiration: Peach, soft and velvety, against the rose-musk base
accords.note_to_perfumer: Soft, velvety peach against a genuine rose-musk-oud attar — the fuzzy-skin lactone facet sitting over Rose Wardia, not a bare oud drydown.

accords.name: Green apple
accords.inspiration: Green apple, sharp against the deep animalic base
accords.note_to_perfumer: Fresh green apple cut sharp against a real rose-oud-musk chord — cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the bitten skin, the full attar depth still underneath rather than a quiet single-note oud.

accords.name: Rose, with berries steeped underneath
accords.inspiration: Rose, with berries steeped underneath — the classic attar move
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia at real strength with blackcurrant steeped underneath — the fruited-rose attar move done honestly, oud and agarwood only a shadow, exactly as a mukhallat should carry them.

accords.name: Bright citrus
accords.inspiration: Bright citrus, unusual against the rose-oud base but real
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bright bergamot and orange laid over the full rose-oud-musk chord — an unusual citrus-attar combination, but built honestly rather than as a plain citrus-oud.

accords.name: A love letter
accords.inspiration: A love letter, the rose ink still wet
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and geraniol at the center, hedione for the ink's own faint sweetness, exaltolide holding it close to skin rather than let it announce itself.

accords.name: Rose
accords.inspiration: Rose, crushed and pressed between the pages of a book
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia flattened against cedarwood and a whisper of vetiver — the exact smell of a real flower dried inside a closed book for years, paper and petal as one note.

accords.name: A wax seal
accords.inspiration: A wax seal, still warm, closing the envelope
accords.note_to_perfumer: Benzoin and labdanum for the warm melted-wax resin, rose just behind it — the moment of sealing something, not the letter itself.

accords.name: Ink and parchment
accords.inspiration: Ink and parchment — nothing living in the room but the letter
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and vetiver for dry paper and old ink, no flower at all — the room the letter was written in, not the rose it describes.

accords.name: A faded photograph
accords.inspiration: A faded photograph, the powder of an old dressing table
accords.note_to_perfumer: Methyl ionone's violet-iris powder standing in for a photograph's own fade, a little benzyl acetate for the ghost of a rose, exaltolide for warm old skin.

accords.name: A poem
accords.inspiration: A poem, handwritten, never sent
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia against a quiet vanilla-benzoin warmth — tender rather than declared, the poem that stayed in the drawer.

accords.name: A candle left burning for someone who isn't coming back
accords.inspiration: A candle left burning for someone who isn't coming back
accords.note_to_perfumer: Benzoin and labdanum for melted wax and grief's own warmth, rose held underneath rather than forward — mourning, not romance exactly, but the same rose.

accords.name: Violets pressed flat
accords.inspiration: Violets pressed flat, years ago, still faintly there
accords.note_to_perfumer: Methyl ionone gamma at real strength for true violet-iris powder, rose only a trace behind it, linalool keeping it from turning heavy.

accords.name: The library where it happened
accords.inspiration: The library where it happened — old paper, and her perfume
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and a trace of patchouli for the library itself, Rose Wardia and hedione carrying the memory of a person through the room.

accords.name: First love
accords.inspiration: First love — bright, a little nervous, rose over clean skin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia lifted by bergamot rather than weighed down by resin, clean galaxolide-exaltolide skin underneath — young, not yet complicated.

accords.name: A dark floral, animalic underneath
accords.inspiration: A dark floral, animalic underneath — not for daylight
accords.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine Sambac against civet at real (if trace) strength — the indolic, slightly rotten edge real jasmine already carries, pushed further rather than smoothed away.

accords.name: Smoke and cold ash
accords.inspiration: Smoke and cold ash, the fire long out
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cypriol and guaiacol for real smoke, patchouli and cedarwood for what's left in the grate afterward. No sweetness anywhere.

accords.name: Skin and leather
accords.inspiration: Skin and leather, worn in, nothing clean about it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Safraleine and civet for the leather itself, norlimbanol for a dry synthetic-timber scratch underneath. Built to feel used, not new.

accords.name: Patchouli taken all the way
accords.inspiration: Patchouli taken all the way, oud underneath
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli at full strength rather than a supporting role, oud and agarwood as the floor underneath it — the 70s-patchouli move updated with a real oud base.

accords.name: A cathedral after mass
accords.inspiration: A cathedral after mass, incense still hanging in the stone
accords.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense and myrrh at real strength, cypriol for the stone itself — cool, elevated smoke rather than a warm gourmand incense.

accords.name: Musk the way it used to mean something
accords.inspiration: Musk the way it used to mean something — animal, not laundry
accords.note_to_perfumer: Civet at real (trace) strength against exaltolide and ethylene brassylate's warmth — the pre-Galaxolide idea of musk, skin rather than clean cotton.

accords.name: Amber taken to its darkest
accords.inspiration: Amber taken to its darkest, most animalic edge
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and oud together rather than labdanum alone, civet at absolute trace pushing the classic amber triangle as dark as this palette allows.

accords.name: Oud with nothing softened
accords.inspiration: Oud with nothing softened — bitter, dry, medicinal
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence at real strength with cypriol's ink and norlimbanol's dry scratch — no rose, no sweetness, nothing to make it easier.

accords.name: Tobacco and old leather
accords.inspiration: Tobacco and old leather, a study lined with both
accords.note_to_perfumer: No true tobacco absolute in this palette, so the hay-and-honey facet is reconstructed from coumarin against patchouli and labdanum's leather — an honest approximation, not a copy.

accords.name: One idea
accords.inspiration: One idea, worked until it needs nothing else
accords.note_to_perfumer: The minimalist 'molecule' niche move — Iso E Super pushed to a real, almost improper dose with only ambroxan and a trace of norlimbanol for company. For someone who wants the idea, not a composition.

accords.name: A cabin
accords.inspiration: A cabin, the fire lit, cedar walls holding the smoke in
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood at real strength with guaiacol's smoke worked in at a bare trace, patchouli and benzoin for the room's own warmth. The whole scene, not just the fire.

accords.name: Pine
accords.inspiration: Pine, straight and cold, nothing else in the air
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pine EO against cedarwood and vetiver rather than a sweetened 'Christmas tree' pine — a real, slightly bitter conifer forest.

formula.bench_warning: below MIN_WEIGHABLE (0.05 g) at 10.0 g batch — use a working dilution or a larger batch

accords.name: Campfire smoke
accords.inspiration: Campfire smoke, caught in a sweater the next morning
accords.note_to_perfumer: Guaiacol at real strength for genuine woodsmoke, cypriol and patchouli underneath, coumarin's hay-sweetness for the marshmallow-adjacent memory.

accords.name: Mountain air
accords.inspiration: Mountain air, thin and cold, before the treeline
accords.note_to_perfumer: Floralozone and dihydromyrcenol for the thin, ozone-cold high-altitude air, pine only a low hum underneath.

accords.name: The forest floor
accords.inspiration: The forest floor — wet leaves, root, and soil
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and vetiver for the damp ground, geosmin at a bare trace for the exact smell of leaf litter after rain, peatmoss for the moss underneath it all.

accords.name: Snow settling on pine
accords.inspiration: Snow settling on pine, cold and clean and green
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pine EO under floralozone and dihydromyrcenol's cold sparkle, galaxolide for the hush snowfall brings rather than silence.

accords.name: The cabin's own walls
accords.inspiration: The cabin's own walls — cedar, and years of woodsmoke
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix at real strength with guaiacol at the barest trace — the structure itself, long after anyone last lit a fire in it.

accords.name: An alpine meadow
accords.inspiration: An alpine meadow — green and floral and short-lived
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clary sage and petitgrain for the meadow's own bitter-green, geraniol and hedione for the wildflowers that only last a few weeks a year up there.

accords.name: Woodsmoke and whiskey
accords.inspiration: Woodsmoke and whiskey — the cabin's other fireplace
accords.note_to_perfumer: Guaiacol's smoke against coumarin and benzoin's warmth — the whiskey poured once everyone's come in from the cold.

accords.name: Something colder and stranger
accords.inspiration: Something colder and stranger — the sky itself, not the ground
accords.note_to_perfumer: Ambroxan and floralozone for something closer to atmosphere than forest — abstract, mineral, the one entry in this set that looks up instead of down.

accords.name: Musk built to still be there tomorrow morning
accords.inspiration: Musk built to still be there tomorrow morning
accords.note_to_perfumer: Exaltolide, habanolide, and ethylene brassylate all at real strength together — three different macrocyclic musks stacked rather than one doing all the work.

accords.name: Amber with a fixative base heavy enough to last the whole day
accords.inspiration: Amber with a fixative base heavy enough to last the whole day
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin's usual amber warmth, but with exaltolide and ethylene brassylate doing the holding instead of relying on the resins alone.

accords.name: Oud with almost nothing volatile left in the formula
accords.inspiration: Oud with almost nothing volatile left in the formula
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence anchored by exaltolide and ethylene brassylate rather than any top note at all — built to survive, not to open beautifully.

accords.name: Skin-musk that survives a shower and comes back that evening
accords.inspiration: Skin-musk that survives a shower and comes back that evening
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bacdanol's creamy sandalwood-musk against exaltolide and ambroxan — the specific 'ghost scent' effect of a fixative this heavy reactivating on warm skin.

accords.name: Citrus
accords.inspiration: Citrus, but engineered to outlast every citrus that came before it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and orange kept deliberately light on top, exaltolide and ethylene brassylate doing all the real work underneath — citrus's oldest problem solved by brute-force fixative rather than a clever trick.

accords.name: A soft
accords.inspiration: A soft, velvet base heavy enough to anchor anything sprayed over it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cashmeran at real strength against Iso E Super and ambroxan — soft, spiced, and built specifically to hold other things down rather than stand alone.

accords.name: Rose that doesn't fade by lunchtime
accords.inspiration: Rose that doesn't fade by lunchtime
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia at real strength held up by exaltolide and ethylene brassylate in equal measure — the flower itself doesn't get to fade first.

accords.name: Vanilla with a fixative base instead of a top-note burst
accords.inspiration: Vanilla with a fixative base instead of a top-note burst
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vanillin and benzoin's usual sweetness, but built on ethylene brassylate and exaltolide rather than a shallow gourmand base that burns off in an hour.

accords.name: A dry wood built entirely around holding power
accords.inspiration: A dry wood built entirely around holding power
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vertofix and vetiver's dry depth locked in with ethylene brassylate and exaltolide — dryness that survives rather than a wood that opens dry and fades soft.

accords.name: The heaviest fixative combination this palette allows
accords.inspiration: The heaviest fixative combination this palette allows
accords.note_to_perfumer: Norlimbanol, ambroxan, exaltolide, and ethylene brassylate together at real strength — the ceiling of what this palette's fixatives can do, all at once.

accords.name: Built to fill the room before you've finished walking into it
accords.inspiration: Built to fill the room before you've finished walking into it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Iso E Super pushed to a genuinely high dose, ambroxan and sylvamber both layered on top for maximum diffusion rather than one projection material carrying the whole formula.

accords.name: Oud pushed outward instead of held close
accords.inspiration: Oud pushed outward instead of held close
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence carried on a heavy Iso E Super and ambroxan base — oud reworked to project rather than sit close to skin the way it usually does.

accords.name: Every projection material this palette has
accords.inspiration: Every projection material this palette has, working together
accords.note_to_perfumer: Sylvamber, ambroxan, and habanolide stacked together — the single loudest combination in the library.

accords.name: Clean
accords.inspiration: Clean, loud, unmistakable the second you walk in
accords.note_to_perfumer: Habanolide and galaxolide both at real strength, hedione for radiance — clean rather than dark, but genuinely loud.

accords.name: Amber that projects instead of sitting close to skin
accords.inspiration: Amber that projects instead of sitting close to skin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin's warmth carried outward on a real Iso E Super and ambroxan dose — the amber accord rebuilt for throw, not intimacy.

accords.name: Spice built to trail behind you down the hallway
accords.inspiration: Spice built to trail behind you down the hallway
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper lifted by a heavy Iso E Super and ambroxan base so the spice itself carries into the next room.

accords.name: A floral loud enough to be a broadcast
accords.inspiration: A floral loud enough to be a broadcast, not a whisper
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and jasmine sambac carried on a genuinely high hedione and Iso E Super dose — the amplifier effect pushed as far as it goes.

accords.name: Dry wood turned into a beacon instead of a background
accords.inspiration: Dry wood turned into a beacon instead of a background
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix under a heavy sylvamber and Iso E Super load — dry wood built to be noticed across a room, not just close up.

accords.name: Sweetness with real throw
accords.inspiration: Sweetness with real throw, not just a close warm skin-scent
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vanillin and benzoin lifted by Iso E Super and ambroxan rather than left to sit quiet and close — sweetness that actually travels.

accords.name: An entrance
accords.inspiration: An entrance, built the way the first line of a symphony is
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and cedarwood together, carried outward on the heaviest Iso E Super and ambroxan dose in the set — the whole library's idea of a proper entrance.

accords.name: A bright burst
accords.inspiration: A bright burst, built to be sprayed again by noon
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and dihydromyrcenol with a real aldehyde C10 sparkle — meant to be vivid for two hours and reapplied rather than stretched thin to survive six.

accords.name: A floral that's just as good the third time as the first
accords.inspiration: A floral that's just as good the third time as the first
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia carried mostly on hedione and floralozone rather than a heavy fixative base — a floral that blooms freshly on each reapplication instead of building up.

accords.name: Rose that wants to be reapplied
accords.inspiration: Rose that wants to be reapplied, not stretched to survive alone
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and geraniol at real, bright strength with almost no heavy base underneath — deliberately built to fade rather than linger, so the ritual of reapplying is the point.

accords.name: A spice burst that tops up clean instead of muddying
accords.inspiration: A spice burst that tops up clean instead of muddying
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and pink pepper over bergamot — a spice top note light enough that a second or third spray never turns muddy the way heavier spice bases can.

accords.name: Citrus that asks for an encore rather than fighting to last
accords.inspiration: Citrus that asks for an encore rather than fighting to last
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot, orange, and petitgrain at full citrus-cologne strength, no attempt made to anchor it — the opposite design choice from The Marathon in the long-lasting set, on purpose.

accords.name: A green burst
accords.inspiration: A green burst, cut and bright, made to be topped up
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cis-3-hexenyl acetate and petitgrain for the cut-green snap, floralozone for air — a green that reads as freshly cut each time, not a single long green note fading.

accords.name: A heady floral that's honestly better sprayed twice
accords.inspiration: A heady floral that's honestly better sprayed twice
accords.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine Sambac and Rose Wardia at real strength on a light hedione-galaxolide base — indolic and heady in the first twenty minutes, which is exactly why it's built to be refreshed rather than left to fade slowly.

accords.name: A sweet top-note burst
accords.inspiration: A sweet top-note burst, not a slow warm drydown
accords.note_to_perfumer: Ethyl maltol and orange for an immediate sugar-citrus burst, no benzoin or heavy resin holding it down — sweetness as a spray-and-repeat event, not an all-day base.

accords.name: A cool splash
accords.inspiration: A cool splash, meant to be reapplied like sunscreen
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dihydromyrcenol, floralozone, and aldehyde C12 MNA at real cologne strength — the classic 'splash' format this whole family belongs to, built to be topped up all day exactly like the sunscreen it's compared to.

accords.name: Everything about this set in one bottle
accords.inspiration: Everything about this set in one bottle, for the committed reapplier
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and bergamot together on a hedione-dihydromyrcenol base — floral, citrus, and aldehydic in even balance, so whichever facet the wearer notices fading, reapplying brings all three back at once.

accords.name: Clean and marine
accords.inspiration: Clean and marine — glassy, like sea-glass, nothing heavy
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dihydromyrcenol and floralozone for the sea-glass sparkle, hedione for the dew, cedarwood and iso E super to keep it from vanishing in twenty minutes. No true marine aldehyde in the palette, so this is built from freshness materials layered rather than one 'ocean' note.

accords.name: Cucumber and melon
accords.inspiration: Cucumber and melon, splashy and green
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cucumber's green snap from cis-3-hexenyl acetate, gamma-undecalactone for a melon-soft roundness — there's no dedicated melon or cucumber material in the palette, so both are reconstructed from adjacent green/fruity facets.

accords.name: Fresh-pressed cotton
accords.inspiration: Fresh-pressed cotton, straight off the line
accords.note_to_perfumer: Fresh-pressed cotton — the classic aldehyde-linalool 'clean laundry' accord, galaxolide for the fabric-softener musk everyone recognizes without naming.

accords.name: Bright citrus over open water
accords.inspiration: Bright citrus over open water
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot and orange over dihydromyrcenol's sparkle — the citrus-cologne structure updated with hedione's transparency instead of a heavier classical base.

accords.name: The same
accords.inspiration: The same, but I want it to actually last past noon
accords.note_to_perfumer: The same marine freshness as Ocean Glass, but anchored — ambroxan, exaltolide, and ethylene brassylate at real strength turn the top notes into an all-day skin-musk instead of a two-hour spray-and-fade.

accords.name: Citrus that doesn't disappear in twenty minutes
accords.inspiration: Citrus that doesn't disappear in twenty minutes
accords.note_to_perfumer: Citrus cologne's oldest problem — it disappears — solved with exaltolide and ethylene brassylate underneath at real dose, so the bergamot keeps reappearing off warm skin for hours instead of fading after the first one.

accords.name: Cool water that dries down into a real
accords.inspiration: Cool water that dries down into a real, long musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: Barely 'fresh' at all by the fourth hour — deliberately. Starts as cool water, dries down into a clean, long-wearing musk that's most of the point.

accords.name: My skin, but cooler
accords.inspiration: My skin, but cooler — and it stays
accords.note_to_perfumer: 'Your skin, but cooler' — hedione's dewy transparency over a genuinely long-wearing musk base. The freshest thing that could plausibly still be there at midnight.

accords.name: Toasted nuts and caramel
accords.inspiration: Toasted nuts and caramel — praline, not candy
accords.note_to_perfumer: Toasted hazelnut-praline built from lactone and coumarin rather than a literal nut note, vanilla and benzoin for warmth, cashmeran and iso E super so it reads as a perfume on skin, not a dessert in a bowl.

accords.name: Salted caramel
accords.inspiration: Salted caramel — sweetness with a mineral edge
accords.note_to_perfumer: Real caramel (ethyl maltol at a careful trace, not a flood) against ambroxan's dry, mineral-salt facet — the salt keeps it from ever turning into pure sugar.

accords.name: Vanilla and tonka
accords.inspiration: Vanilla and tonka, done properly, at real strength
accords.note_to_perfumer: The modern tonka-vanilla done at full strength — real vanillin and coumarin, not a compromise dose, held up by iso E super and cashmeran so it stays elegant instead of collapsing into sweetness.

accords.name: Rose and honeyed pastry
accords.inspiration: Rose and honeyed pastry — floral first, dessert second
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose water and honeyed phyllo — Rose Wardia leads, gamma-nonalactone and benzyl acetate for the honey-almond syrup, cardamom threaded through. Dessert-adjacent, but rose stays the point.

accords.name: Something boozy
accords.inspiration: Something boozy — whiskey, oak, nothing that reads as candy
accords.note_to_perfumer: A boozy, grown-up gourmand — guaiacol at real trace for the charred-oak-barrel note, patchouli for the cask's depth, coumarin and benzoin for the whiskey's own sweetness. Nothing here reads as candy.

accords.name: Iced coffee and vanilla
accords.inspiration: Iced coffee and vanilla — cool, not warm
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cold-brew coffee and vanilla, cooled down instead of warmed up — dihydromyrcenol for the ice, coffee CO2 kept light rather than roasty. A summer gourmand, not a winter one.

accords.name: Vanilla
accords.inspiration: Vanilla — soft and sweet, not sharp
accords.note_to_perfumer: Real vanilla and benzoin wrapped around oud and agarwood — soft and sweet, never sharp, with ethyl maltol at the barest trace so it stays perfume and not dessert.

accords.name: Amber
accords.inspiration: Amber — resin and warmth around it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and frankincense wrapped tight around a double-oud core (Agarwood Artessence + Oud Oliffac) — ambroxan for lift, less sweet than a full mukhallat amber, more resin than musk.

accords.name: Nothing — just make it darker
accords.inspiration: Nothing — just make it darker. Animalic, heavy, real
accords.note_to_perfumer: As dark as the palette goes — civet at absolute trace for real animal warmth, norlimbanol and cypriol for a dry, smoke-adjacent leather, double oud underneath. Not for daylight.

accords.name: Spice
accords.inspiration: Spice — cardamom and pepper worked into it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper as an accent, not the main event — oud and agarwood stay the center, safraleine bridging the two.

accords.name: Something fresh
accords.inspiration: Something fresh — I don't want it to feel heavy at all
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud kept deliberately light — bergamot, petitgrain, and dihydromyrcenol do most of the talking, agarwood only a low hum underneath. For the customer who wants oud's idea, not its weight.

accords.name: Something sparkling
accords.inspiration: Something sparkling — almost fizzy, like it's carbonated
accords.note_to_perfumer: The 'sparkling' modern-niche trend, built honestly: aldehyde C10 and C12 for the metallic fizz, dihydromyrcenol and bergamot for the citrus pop, blackcurrant for a cola-adjacent soda note — all of it sitting on top of a dark oud base it never actually dissolves into.

accords.name: Dry
accords.inspiration: Dry, mineral, almost salty
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dry, mineral, almost salty — ambroxan and vetiver instead of the usual sweet resins. The amber family's driest possible reading.

accords.name: Dark
accords.inspiration: Dark, leathery, honeyed
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dark, leathery, honeyed — labdanum and safraleine for the leather, civet at absolute trace for real warmth, benzoin so it never turns dry. The amber a saddle would smell like.

accords.name: Sweet
accords.inspiration: Sweet, powdery, vanillic
accords.note_to_perfumer: Sweet, powdery, unapologetically vanillic — vanillin and benzoin at real strength, coumarin for the powder, labdanum keeping it from turning into dessert.

accords.name: Dense and animalic
accords.inspiration: Dense and animalic — amber with an oud shadow
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac leads.

accords.name: Honeyed and thick
accords.inspiration: Honeyed and thick, almost edible without tipping into dessert
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin pushed to their thickest, most honeyed edge — ethyl maltol at a bare trace for sweetness, civet at homeopathic trace for warmth, without ever tipping into gourmand.

accords.name: Smoky and churchy
accords.inspiration: Smoky and churchy — frankincense and myrrh leading, not labdanum
accords.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense and myrrh lead instead of the usual labdanum-benzoin pair — smoky and resinous, closer to a censer than a bottle.

accords.name: Floral amber
accords.inspiration: Floral amber — rose and jasmine folded into the resin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose and jasmine folded into the classic labdanum-benzoin base — the warmth still leads, but there's a real floral heart inside it now, not just a hint.

accords.name: Spiced amber
accords.inspiration: Spiced amber — cardamom and pepper running through the resin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom and black pepper cut into the resin the way they would in a real oud-and-amber attar — spice as texture, not garnish.

accords.name: Fresh amber
accords.inspiration: Fresh amber — a citrus top over the resin, lighter and more modern
accords.note_to_perfumer: A citrus top laid over the same labdanum-benzoin base, ambroxan instead of a heavier resin for the drydown — the modern, lighter reading of amber.

accords.name: Dark berries
accords.inspiration: Dark berries — blackcurrant, jammy over warm resin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dark berries over a warm labdanum-benzoin amber — blackcurrant and damascone's jammy top, iso E super for lift, no oud underneath at all.

accords.name: Mango
accords.inspiration: Mango, ripe and creamy, melting into the amber
accords.note_to_perfumer: Creamy tropical mango melted straight into the amber's own sweetness — gamma-undecalactone and fructone for the fruit, vanillin rounding it out, nothing woody enough to compete.

accords.name: Peach
accords.inspiration: Peach, soft and velvety, warmed by the resin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Soft, velvety peach warmed by labdanum and benzoin rather than cooled by oud — the fuzzy-skin lactone facet sitting directly in the resin.

accords.name: Green apple
accords.inspiration: Green apple, cutting sharp through the sweetness
accords.note_to_perfumer: Fresh green apple cut sharp against the amber's warmth — cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the bitten skin, bergamot to lift it, the resin still doing most of the talking underneath.

accords.name: Rose
accords.inspiration: Rose, with berries steeped underneath it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia and blackcurrant steeped into the labdanum-benzoin base — a floral-fruity amber, no oud shadow the way the mukhallat version carries one.

accords.name: Bright citrus cutting through all that resin
accords.inspiration: Bright citrus cutting through all that resin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bright bergamot and orange cutting straight through the resin — the amber kept warm and thick underneath rather than reduced to a whisper.

accords.name: Classic
accords.inspiration: Classic — bergamot, rose, and a mossy floor, the true triangle
accords.note_to_perfumer: The chypre triangle at its most textbook — bergamot's top, rose and jasmine's heart, patchouli and peatmoss standing in for oakmoss, labdanum for warmth. The reference the other nine bend away from.

accords.name: Fruity
accords.inspiration: Fruity — a peach-plum facet running under the moss, like the classics did it
accords.note_to_perfumer: Beta-damascone and gamma-undecalactone stand in for the peach-plum facet the old aldehyde-fruity chypres built around — a jammy fruit note worked into the moss, not sprayed on top of it.

accords.name: Floral
accords.inspiration: Floral — rose and jasmine take over, the moss goes quiet
accords.note_to_perfumer: The floral heart pulled all the way forward — rose and jasmine at real strength, the mossy base still there but reduced to a floor, not a competing voice.

accords.name: Leather
accords.inspiration: Leather — dark, animalic, closer to a cuir than a floral
accords.note_to_perfumer: Civet at absolute trace and a heavier labdanum/patchouli base turn the chypre leathery and dark — the floral heart still present but demoted, this reads as cuir first.

accords.name: Aldehydic
accords.inspiration: Aldehydic — sparkling top, powdery heart, the vintage move
accords.note_to_perfumer: Two aldehydes at the top open it sparkling and slightly soapy before a rose-and-methyl-ionone heart settles in over the mossy floor — the classic vintage aldehyde-chypre move.

accords.name: Woody
accords.inspiration: Woody — patchouli and cedar forward, drier than the floral read
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and cedar pushed past the floral heart entirely — dry and mossy, the floral reduced to a supporting hedione facet rather than a named note.

accords.name: Spicy
accords.inspiration: Spicy — pepper and clove worked into the moss
accords.note_to_perfumer: Black pepper and clove bud cut into the mossy floor — spice as an accent inside the chypre structure, not its own layer on top.

formula.bench_warning: below MIN_WEIGHABLE (0.05 g) at 10.0 g batch — use a working dilution or a larger batch

accords.name: Fresh
accords.inspiration: Fresh — a lighter, more citrus-forward chypre, less moss
accords.note_to_perfumer: The moss cut back hard and the citrus doubled — a chypre built to feel light and bright rather than dense and dark.

accords.name: Amber
accords.inspiration: Amber — the base gone warm and resinous, closer to an ambery chypre
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and benzoin pushed well past the classic ratio — the mossy floor stays, but the whole base leans warm and resinous instead of dry and green.

accords.name: Clean
accords.inspiration: Clean — a modern skin-musk chypre, the moss barely a memory
accords.note_to_perfumer: The classic triangle reduced to its outline — moss and patchouli barely present, clean musks doing what the base used to do. A chypre for someone who wants the shape without the weight.

accords.name: Classic
accords.inspiration: Classic — lavender, hay, oakmoss, nothing modern about it
accords.note_to_perfumer: The fougère as it was invented — lavender and hay against oakmoss and moss-root, nothing softened for modern taste. The reference the other nine bend away from.

accords.name: Fresh
accords.inspiration: Fresh — citrus and lavender, barely there base
accords.note_to_perfumer: Lighter-handed than the classic build — citrus pushed forward, the oakmoss floor barely there, coumarin cut back so it never turns sweet.

accords.name: Woody
accords.inspiration: Woody — vetiver and cedar doing the talking, dry all the way down
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver and cedar take over from the lavender — dry, rooty, closer to a woody-aromatic than a soft fougère.

accords.name: Spicy
accords.inspiration: Spicy — pepper and geranium sharpening the lavender
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pepper and geranium worked into the lavender's own spice-facet rather than layered on top of it — the fougère read through a spicier lens.

accords.name: Sweet
accords.inspiration: Sweet — tonka and vanilla pushed forward, the modern gourmand read
accords.note_to_perfumer: The 'fougère gourmande' move — tonka's own sweetness pulled out and amplified with vanillin and benzoin until the hay note reads more dessert than herb.

accords.name: Aquatic
accords.inspiration: Aquatic — a marine facet laid over the lavender-hay handshake
accords.note_to_perfumer: The 90s aromatic-aquatic move — dihydromyrcenol and floralozone laid over the same lavender-coumarin spine, sea air instead of hay.

accords.name: Leather
accords.inspiration: Leather — patchouli and a dark base under the lavender
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli and labdanum turn the base leathery and dark — the lavender now sits on top of something closer to a chypre's mossy floor than a clean fougère base.

accords.name: Green
accords.inspiration: Green — sharp, bitter, almost savage
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clary sage and cis-3-hexenyl acetate push the green facet as sharp and bitter as this palette allows — the aromatic side of fougère, none of the softness.

accords.name: Amber
accords.inspiration: Amber — the base gone warm and resinous instead of mossy
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oakmoss's usual dry-moss floor swapped for labdanum and frankincense — warmer and more resinous, the fougère read through an amber lens.

accords.name: Clean
accords.inspiration: Clean — modern minimalist, mostly musk and air
accords.note_to_perfumer: The lavender and hay reduced to a whisper, everything else stripped back to clean skin-musk — a fougère for someone who wants the shape of one without any of its volume.

accords.name: The swing by the tree
accords.inspiration: The swing by the tree
accords.note_to_perfumer: Sun-hot rope, bark, dust, and something sweet from far off. Cedarwood + cypriol + a lactone whisper. Dry, never wet.

accords.name: Bidaai
accords.inspiration: Bidaai. The car door closing
accords.note_to_perfumer: Flowers going over, exhaust, someone's perfume leaving the room. Overblown rose + jasmine, a metallic aldehyde edge, musk that outlasts them both.

accords.name: Kewra sherbet
accords.inspiration: Kewra sherbet, passed around in small steel glasses
accords.note_to_perfumer: Attar Kewra — the real pandanus-flower attar, sweet and slightly medicinal-green — with rose and a whisper of cardamom, exactly how the sherbet tastes at a wedding. Benzoin rounds the sweetness so it isn't just syrup.

accords.name: Classic Amber
accords.inspiration: Classic Amber
accords.note_to_perfumer: The amber accord's textbook form: labdanum + benzoin + vanillin. Everything else in this library that reads as 'amber' is a variation on this triangle.

accords.name: Petrichor Backbone
accords.inspiration: Petrichor Backbone
accords.note_to_perfumer: Attar Mitti — the genuine Kannauj clay attar — supplies the ground, geosmin the trace lift of the moment rain lands, floralozone the air just before, cis-3-hexenyl acetate the crushed grass. The standard rain build across this whole library, now with the real material at its base instead of a synthetic reconstruction alone.

accords.name: Mukhallat Triangle
accords.inspiration: Mukhallat Triangle
accords.note_to_perfumer: Oud Oliffac + Agarwood Artessence + Rose Wardia + Safraleine. The rose-oud-saffron axis that anchors every Middle Eastern-coded path in the graph, now with a rounder agarwood chord behind the sharper oud reconstruction.

accords.name: Chypre Floor
accords.inspiration: Chypre Floor
accords.note_to_perfumer: The full chypre triangle now, not just the base — bergamot's top, rose and jasmine's heart, peatmoss and patchouli standing in for oakmoss, labdanum for warmth. Not restricted the way true oakmoss is.

accords.name: Fougère Spine
accords.inspiration: Fougère Spine
accords.note_to_perfumer: Lavandin Grosso + coumarin, now standing on a real base — peatmoss and vetiver for oakmoss, galaxolide and iso E super to hold it together. The lavender-hay handshake that every fougère in history is built from, the real lavender now, not linalyl acetate standing in for it.

accords.name: The Aunties' Perfume
accords.inspiration: The Aunties' Perfume
accords.note_to_perfumer: Aldehyde C-10 + C-12 MNA over rose and galaxolide. Mid-century aldehydic glamour — sharp, unforgettable, dressed for a wedding.

accords.name: Old Cupboard / Shawl
accords.inspiration: Old Cupboard / Shawl
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cashmeran blurs spice into wood so neither reads separately, methyl ionone gamma ages it, benzoin gives it the sweet dust of a closed drawer.

accords.name: Ink and Parchment
accords.inspiration: Ink and Parchment
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coffee CO2 at micro-dose reads as ink, not coffee. Guaiacol's smoke meets it — the archive-room accord.

accords.name: Skin Musk Classic
accords.inspiration: Skin Musk Classic
accords.note_to_perfumer: Exaltolide for warmth, Ambroxan for radiance, Galaxolide for cushion. The three-musk skeleton behind almost every base in this library.

accords.name: Dry Wood Spine
accords.inspiration: Dry Wood Spine
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood for structure, Iso E Super for air, Vertofix for shadow. The library-and-desk wood floor.

accords.name: Kitchen Dairy Sweet
accords.inspiration: Kitchen Dairy Sweet
accords.note_to_perfumer: Gamma nonalactone and delta decalactone for milk, vanillin to round it. Kulfi and kheer live here.

accords.name: Bright Citrus Morning
accords.inspiration: Bright Citrus Morning

accords.name: Hot Spice Ceremony
accords.inspiration: Hot Spice Ceremony

accords.name: Smoked Vanilla
accords.inspiration: Smoked Vanilla

accords.name: Forest Honey
accords.inspiration: Forest Honey

accords.name: Royal Oriental Dessert
accords.inspiration: Royal Oriental Dessert

accords.name: Rose Ghazal
accords.inspiration: Rose Ghazal
accords.note_to_perfumer: A true rose, not a rose-adjacent facet — Rose Wardia and geraniol at the center, jasmine sambac for depth, exaltolide for the skin-warm musk that makes it wearable rather than just a rose oil.

accords.name: Desert Oud
accords.inspiration: Desert Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dark oud and agarwood over dry cypriol ink and patchouli — animalic, resinous, built to last on skin rather than to project loudly.

accords.name: Masala Nights
accords.inspiration: Masala Nights
accords.note_to_perfumer: A full spice-market oriental — cardamom, pink pepper, and clove over cedarwood and labdanum, safraleine for a leather-saffron thread. Wear this, don't just smell the spice rack.

accords.name: Citron et Fleurs
accords.inspiration: Citron et Fleurs
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bright bergamot and orange over a soft musky-woody skin — a real cologne structure, not a citrus top note alone.

accords.name: Cuir Sauvage
accords.inspiration: Cuir Sauvage
accords.note_to_perfumer: Leather built the honest way — civet at absolute trace for life, safraleine and norlimbanol for the leather-suede dryness, cypriol's ink and patchouli's depth underneath.

accords.name: Skin Musk
accords.inspiration: Skin Musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clean skin-musk — no single note announces itself, just warmth and a sense that you smell like a better version of yourself up close.

accords.name: Fresh Musk
accords.inspiration: Fresh Musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clean skin-musk with real citrus lift — bergamot and petitgrain keep it from ever feeling heavy, dihydromyrcenol for the cool sparkle. Musk you'd wear in daylight.

accords.name: Spiced Musk
accords.inspiration: Spiced Musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: Warm skin-musk threaded with cardamom, black pepper, and nutmeg — spice as a texture on the musk, not a top note fighting it.

accords.name: Classic Fougère
accords.inspiration: Classic Fougère
accords.note_to_perfumer: The classical structure done properly, at full strength — real lavender (Lavandin Grosso, not linalyl acetate alone) against coumarin's hay-sweetness, peatmoss and patchouli standing in for oakmoss, galaxolide holding the whole thing together. Barbershop, elevated.

accords.name: Floral Chypre
accords.inspiration: Floral Chypre
accords.note_to_perfumer: The true chypre triangle at full strength — bergamot's top, rose and jasmine's heart, patchouli and peatmoss standing in for oakmoss at the base, labdanum for warmth. A perfume in three acts, the way chypre always was.

accords.name: Velvet Musk Oud
accords.inspiration: Velvet Musk Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: A musk-forward mukhallat — exaltolide and habanolide's clean skin-musk wrapped around a soft, understated oud.

accords.name: Jasmine Royal
accords.inspiration: Jasmine Royal
accords.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine sambac carried on hedione's dewy lift — oud and agarwood are only a shadow behind the flower here.

accords.name: Oriental Honey
accords.inspiration: Oriental Honey
accords.note_to_perfumer: Honeyed benzoin and tonka over a soft oud-amber base — the sweetest of the mukhallats, but never a dessert.

accords.name: Black Royal
accords.inspiration: Black Royal
accords.note_to_perfumer: The darkest of the set — cypriol's ink and patchouli's depth under a heavy double-oud (Agarwood Artessence + Oud Oliffac), norlimbanol for a dry, near-silent woody floor.

accords.name: Palace Nights
accords.inspiration: Palace Nights
accords.note_to_perfumer: The full mukhallat chord in one bottle — rose and jasmine over a resinous amber-oud base. If you only try one, try this.

accords.name: Grape Oud
accords.inspiration: Grape Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: Sweet purple grape — methyl anthranilate's candied-grape facet — balanced by a restrained oud and agarwood base.

accords.name: Plum Oud
accords.inspiration: Plum Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dark, jammy plum over earthy patchouli and oud — the richest and darkest of the fruity ouds.

accords.name: Fig Oud
accords.inspiration: Fig Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: Green, milky fig skin over a sophisticated woody-oud base — vetiver for the fig-leaf bitterness.

accords.name: Royal Tropical Oud
accords.inspiration: Royal Tropical Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bright tropical fruit that gradually gives way to creamy oud — the most 'modern mainstream' of the fruity ouds.

accords.name: Black Tea Amber
accords.inspiration: Black Tea Amber
accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot for the earl-grey top, a honeyed lactone facet standing in for the tea itself, labdanum and benzoin for the amber warmth underneath. Tea and honey, not tea and sugar.

accords.name: Toasted Coconut
accords.inspiration: Toasted Coconut
accords.note_to_perfumer: Note honestly: there's no true coconut aromachemical in the current palette, so this reconstructs the toasted-coconut impression from gamma-nonalactone's creamy lactone character plus vanilla and benzoin's warmth — worth a dedicated coconut lactone (e.g. massoia or coconut aldehyde) if this becomes a hero scent.

accords.name: Chai Latte
accords.inspiration: Chai Latte
accords.note_to_perfumer: A full-strength chai — cardamom, black pepper, and nutmeg worked properly into the vanilla-tonka base, not just floating on top of it. The mukhallat 'Masala Chai' accord's more polished, full-perfume sibling.

accords.name: Amber Cashmere
accords.inspiration: Amber Cashmere
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cashmeran as the whole point — soft, spiced woody-amber that reads as a cashmere sweater more than a dessert, vanillin only a hush underneath.

accords.name: Mountain Spring
accords.inspiration: Mountain Spring
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pine and vetiver for the cold mineral water over stone, floralozone and dihydromyrcenol for the air above it. Genuinely cold, not just 'clean'.

accords.name: Glacier Air
accords.inspiration: Glacier Air
accords.note_to_perfumer: As cold as the palette can go without a literal 'ice' accord — aldehyde C10 and floralozone for the thin high-altitude air, cedarwood and ambroxan keeping it from feeling empty.

accords.name: White Tea Mist
accords.inspiration: White Tea Mist
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pale, translucent — hedione carries almost the whole accord, a whisper of bergamot and linalool, floralozone for the mist. The lightest thing in this whole library.

accords.name: Morning Dew
accords.inspiration: Morning Dew
accords.note_to_perfumer: Grass and dew before the sun's properly up — cis-3-hexenyl acetate and hedione, geraniol for a single drop of flower.

accords.name: Bamboo Rain
accords.inspiration: Bamboo Rain
accords.note_to_perfumer: The modern 'bamboo' niche accord — green and hollow-stemmed, petitgrain and vetiver for the stalk, no floral heart at all.

accords.name: Sea Salt Skin
accords.inspiration: Sea Salt Skin
accords.note_to_perfumer: Salt on warm skin after the sea — ambroxan for the mineral-salt facet, hedione and galaxolide so it reads as skin rather than a splash of cologne.

accords.name: Glacier Anchor
accords.inspiration: Glacier Anchor
accords.note_to_perfumer: Glacier Air's icy open, but built onto a proper woody-amber base — cashmeran and ambroxan hold the cold air in place instead of letting it evaporate.

accords.name: Marine Vetiver
accords.inspiration: Marine Vetiver
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver's own natural tenacity does most of the longevity work here — it's one of the few naturally long-wearing fresh materials — dihydromyrcenol and bergamot for the aquatic top, ambroxan bridging the two.

accords.name: Rain Fixed
accords.inspiration: Rain Fixed
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rain's opening, fixed permanently in place — cashmeran and ambroxan hold the petrichor-adjacent trace long past when the real thing would have dried.

accords.name: Sea Breeze Amber
accords.inspiration: Sea Breeze Amber
accords.note_to_perfumer: A fresh top note that drops straight into amber instead of clean musk — labdanum's warmth underneath the sea-breeze opening.

accords.name: Frozen Musk
accords.inspiration: Frozen Musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: Aldehydic sparkle at the very top, then almost entirely musk — designed to feel 'frozen' in place rather than evolving through a normal pyramid.

accords.name: Aquatic Oud
accords.inspiration: Aquatic Oud
accords.note_to_perfumer: A fresh, watery top over a real oud base instead of the usual clean musk — an unusual pairing, but oud's own longevity is exactly what a 'lasting freshness' needs.

accords.name: Noor Mahal
accords.inspiration: Noor Mahal
accords.note_to_perfumer: Palace of Light — Rose Wardia and saffron-adjacent Safraleine catching morning light through a jali screen, aldehydes for the marble-court sparkle, oud and agarwood only a low murmur beneath.

accords.name: Shahi Ittar
accords.inspiration: Shahi Ittar
accords.note_to_perfumer: The royal ittar at its heaviest and most ceremonial — Oud Oliffac and Agarwood Artessence at real strength under Rose Wardia, Safraleine threading saffron-leather through the whole chord, civet at absolute trace for real court-attar warmth.

accords.name: Anarkali
accords.inspiration: Anarkali
accords.note_to_perfumer: Named for the legendary courtesan — Jasmine Sambac and Rose Wardia at the heart, a honeyed benzoin warmth underneath for old-world romance, Exaltolide's skin-musk keeping it close rather than announced.

accords.name: Zafran Bahar
accords.inspiration: Zafran Bahar
accords.note_to_perfumer: Saffron Spring — Safraleine's saffron-leather facet pushed to the front, cardamom and rose just behind it, a thread of honeyed warmth underneath. The spice market and the rose garden in one breath.

accords.name: Takht-e-Ambar
accords.inspiration: Takht-e-Ambar
accords.note_to_perfumer: Amber Throne — the imperial amber at full strength: labdanum, benzoin, and frankincense built up the way a throne room's incense settles into stone over a century, oud and agarwood the shadow underneath it all.

accords.name: Gulab-e-Jahangir
accords.inspiration: Gulab-e-Jahangir
accords.note_to_perfumer: After Nur Jahan's court discovery of rose oil rising to the surface of a canal of rosewater — the purest rose this palette can build: Rose Wardia and geraniol at real strength, phenyl ethyl alcohol for the true rose-petal facet, nothing else allowed to compete.

accords.name: Chandni Raat
accords.inspiration: Chandni Raat
accords.note_to_perfumer: Moonlit Night — jasmine sambac cooled by aldehydes and dihydromyrcenol into something closer to marble and moonlight than a daytime garden, clean musk underneath standing in for the still night air over a reflecting pool.

accords.name: Sandal-e-Khaas
accords.inspiration: Sandal-e-Khaas
accords.note_to_perfumer: Special Sandalwood — no true santalol in this palette, so the creamy, milky sandalwood impression is built honestly from Ebanol and Bacdanol's own sandalwood-adjacent character, cashmeran for the powder, musk underneath for skin-warmth rather than incense-dryness.

accords.name: Mumtaz
accords.inspiration: Mumtaz
accords.note_to_perfumer: For the empress the Taj Mahal was built for — a tender, unhurried rose-jasmine chord with none of Shahi Ittar's density, Bacdanol and Exaltolide keeping it soft and close rather than grand. Devotion, not spectacle.

accords.name: Ranthambore Musk
accords.inspiration: Ranthambore Musk
accords.note_to_perfumer: The royal hunting grounds, not the palace — patchouli and vetiver for the forest floor, civet at absolute trace for real animal presence, cypriol's ink underneath. Wild, not ceremonial.

accords.name: Kannauj Mitti
accords.inspiration: Kannauj Mitti
accords.note_to_perfumer: The classic attar of earth, from the tradition Kannauj is named for — real Attar Mitti (the genuine Kannauj clay attar) at its fullest, geosmin for the exact instant rain lands, nothing floral or woody allowed to distract from it.

accords.name: Mogra Raat
accords.inspiration: Mogra Raat
accords.note_to_perfumer: Mogra — Indian jasmine sambac — at night-blooming intensity, strung like a temple garland. Hedione for the dew; nothing else allowed to compete with the flower itself.

accords.name: Khus Bagicha
accords.inspiration: Khus Bagicha
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver Garden — khus, the way it's known across Indian summers in cooling sherbets and hand-fans as much as in perfume. Vetiver EO and cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the cut-grass-and-root freshness, cedarwood underneath for depth.

accords.name: Marigold Mandir
accords.inspiration: Marigold Mandir
accords.note_to_perfumer: Marigold Temple — no true tagetes note in this palette, so the bright, slightly bitter-green marigold impression is reconstructed honestly from clary sage and petitgrain against a warm, incense-adjacent woody base, cardamom for the offering-tray spice.

accords.name: Sandalwood Sabha
accords.inspiration: Sandalwood Sabha
accords.note_to_perfumer: Sandalwood Assembly — a meditative, single-minded sandalwood built from Ebanol and Bacdanol's creamy facets since true santalol isn't in this palette (see also Sandal-e-Khaas, its more ceremonial Mughal-court sibling), iso E super for lift, nothing sweet allowed to intrude.

accords.name: Henna Sandhya
accords.inspiration: Henna Sandhya
accords.note_to_perfumer: Henna Evening — the green, tannic, faintly medicinal smell of fresh henna paste drying on skin during a mehendi ceremony, reconstructed from clary sage and cis-3-hexenyl acetate's bitter-green facets, warmed by a musky-earthy base rather than left raw.

accords.name: Paan Patti
accords.inspiration: Paan Patti
accords.note_to_perfumer: Betel leaf — an unusual, genuinely under-explored accord in Western perfumery. The sharp, green, faintly medicinal bite of paan reconstructed from clary sage and petitgrain, cardamom and clove for the spiced areca-nut filling, nothing sweet.

accords.name: Agarbatti Dhuni
accords.inspiration: Agarbatti Dhuni
accords.note_to_perfumer: Temple incense-stick smoke — frankincense and myrrh for the resin, cypriol for the dry, ink-like smoke, patchouli underneath for the ash that settles into stone. Built dry and dusty, the way a decades-old temple smells.

accords.name: Nariyal Attar
accords.inspiration: Nariyal Attar
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coconut — the warm, milky-sweet oil of temple prasad and everyday hair-oil culture, not the toasted-dessert reading (see Toasted Coconut in the gourmand set). No true coconut lactone in this palette, so it's built from gamma-nonalactone's creamy character paired with sandalwood-adjacent Ebanol rather than vanilla, keeping it warm-oily instead of bakery-sweet.

accords.name: Chameli Bageecha
accords.inspiration: Chameli Bageecha
accords.note_to_perfumer: Jasmine Garden — chameli, the daytime-garden jasmine variety, brighter and greener than Mogra Raat's heady night-blooming version. Bergamot and petitgrain for the morning light, cis-3-hexenyl acetate for the leaf.

accords.name: Scheherazade
accords.inspiration: Scheherazade
accords.note_to_perfumer: The storyteller herself — Rose Wardia carrying a thousand nights of tales, a honeyed benzoin-vanilla warmth threaded through with Safraleine's saffron-leather, oud only a low undertone. Captivating rather than overwhelming — she has to be asked back tomorrow night.

accords.name: Sultan's Lamp
accords.inspiration: Sultan's Lamp
accords.note_to_perfumer: The genie's lamp, rubbed once — a golden, smoky amber built from labdanum and frankincense, ambroxan for the sudden shimmer of something summoned, oud underneath for weight. Magic with real gravity.

accords.name: Bazaar-e-Layl
accords.inspiration: Bazaar-e-Layl
accords.note_to_perfumer: Night Bazaar — cardamom, black pepper, and saffron-leather Safraleine over a dark, musky base, the way a spice caravan's stalls still smell of the day's trade long after the sun goes down.

accords.name: Desert Rose Mirage
accords.inspiration: Desert Rose Mirage
accords.note_to_perfumer: A rose that shouldn't be able to grow where it does — Rose Wardia held up against dry cypriol and vetiver instead of a lush green stem, the contrast doing the work a mirage does: something soft appearing where the ground promises nothing but sand.

accords.name: Frankincense Caravan
accords.inspiration: Frankincense Caravan
accords.note_to_perfumer: The old trade route itself — frankincense and myrrh at full strength, the two resins this entire trans-Arabian trade was built on, cypriol for the desert dust that never quite washes off the caravan's robes.

accords.name: Date Palm Nectar
accords.inspiration: Date Palm Nectar
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dates at an oasis, not a candy counter — no true date-fruit note exists in this palette, so the sticky, caramelized-fruit impression is built from gamma-undecalactone and delta-decalactone's dried-fruit lactone character against benzoin's warmth, musk underneath for the desert-skin base. Worth a dedicated date accord if this becomes a hero scent.

accords.name: Genie's Veil
accords.inspiration: Genie's Veil
accords.note_to_perfumer: Something seen through gauze, not directly — aldehydes and floralozone for the shimmer, a soft jasmine-adjacent hedione underneath, clean musk holding the whole veil together rather than any one note announcing itself.

accords.name: Palace of a Thousand Nights
accords.inspiration: Palace of a Thousand Nights
accords.note_to_perfumer: The grand finale — every register of the set in one bottle: Rose Wardia and jasmine for the palace gardens, a double oud (Agarwood Artessence + Oud Oliffac) and labdanum for the throne room, benzoin and vanillin for the sweetness woven through it all. The richest, most complete composition here.

accords.name: Midnight Oasis
accords.inspiration: Midnight Oasis
accords.note_to_perfumer: The desert's day/night contrast in one accord — jasmine sambac cool as the temperature drops after sunset, a warm sand-dune musk base rising underneath as the flower fades. Two moments in one bottle.

accords.name: Sinbad's Voyage
accords.inspiration: Sinbad's Voyage
accords.note_to_perfumer: The trade-route voyages, not the palace — bergamot and orange for open water and sun, cardamom and pepper for the spice cargo below deck, cedarwood and vetiver for the ship's own timber. Adventure, not opulence.

accords.name: Treasure Chest
accords.inspiration: Buried in an old chest, wood and leather
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood and Vertofix for dry, worn wood; Oud Oliffac for the leather hinges; Norlimbanol underneath for a dry animalic-amber shadow; Safraleine at a low dose for the spice that got sealed in and never quite left.

accords.name: Raised From the Deep
accords.inspiration: Just pulled up from underwater — wet, briny, barnacled
accords.note_to_perfumer: Ambroxan for the salty, mineral amber radiance; Geosmin at trace for wet stone; Peatmoss for damp, algae-dark shade; Floralozone for the ozonic brine on top; Vetiver EO for the wet root underneath. Nothing here should read dry.

accords.name: The Treasure Map
accords.inspiration: An old map, ink fading on the parchment
accords.note_to_perfumer: Methyl Ionone Gamma is the parchment itself — powdery orris, dry and slightly suede. Cedarwood for the pencil-line dryness, Cypriol at a low dose for the ink, Coumarin for the hay-dust sweetness, Frankincense for the cool dust in the air above it. Keep this one dry — no dew, no wet paper.

accords.name: Paper Money
accords.inspiration: Stacks of old paper money
accords.note_to_perfumer: Galaxolide is the cotton-linen banknote paper itself — clean, slightly powdery, never soapy. Aldehyde C-12 MNA adds the crisp, faintly metallic edge of a freshly counted stack. Cypriol at a very low dose for the ink; Methyl Ionone Gamma for dry powder underneath.

accords.name: Loose Change
accords.inspiration: A handful of coins, cold in your palm
accords.note_to_perfumer: Aldehyde C-10 and Aldehyde C-12 MNA together give the sharp, cold metallic sparkle — the closest this palette gets to the smell coins leave on skin. Dihydromyrcenol adds a soapy-metal edge; Ambroxan underneath keeps it from reading as pure cleaning product by giving it a mineral, skin-warm base.

accords.name: Gold and Jewels
accords.inspiration: Gold and jewels, catching the light
accords.note_to_perfumer: Labdanum and Benzoin melt into the warm, honeyed amber this whole accord is built around. Ethylene Brassylate adds a genuinely golden musk radiance. Safraleine for a jeweled saffron-leather warmth, Frankincense for a cool resinous shimmer so it never tips fully into dessert.

accords.name: The Last Look Back
accords.inspiration: The last look back, before you leave
accords.note_to_perfumer: Iso E Super leads, Exaltolide Total + Cedarwood support. You always look back once. This time it's just an empty room, and somehow that's the part you remember.

Underneath it, cardamom and saffron for the pot already on the stove, guaiacol at trace for the seared edge of frying spice, a ghee-rich lactone for the fat in the pan, and civet at an almost-nothing dose for the savoury depth no gourmand accord usually bothers with. accords.name: Attar Bazaar
accords.inspiration: Oud, saffron and resin — the souk an hour after sundown.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom Oil RCO leads, Pink Pepper + Safraleine + Jasmine Sambac + Oud Oliffac + Labdanum Resinoid (50% in BB) + Ambroxan (10% DPG) support. Built the way a mukhallat is built — no alcohol, no filler, oil layered on oil until it stops smelling like ingredients. Saffron and cardamom sit on top for the first half hour; underneath, oud and labdanum do not move for the rest of the day. It is loud in the way old Gulf perfumery is loud: not sharp, just unmistakably present.

accords.inspiration: Benzoin and frankincense melted into honey and left in the sun.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Orange 10-fold Oil leads, Frankincense (Olibanum) + Benzoin Resinoid 70 DEP (diluted 50% in BB) + Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Labdanum Resinoid (50% in BB) + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. An amber that leans sweet rather than smoky. Benzoin and vanillin are doing most of the work, with frankincense keeping it from turning into dessert. It sits close for the first hour and then blooms — most people notice it on you before you do.

accords.name: Smoke Over the Souk

Guaiacol is nearly pure smoke, and used carelessly it smells like an accident. Here it sits under frankincense and cypriol so it reads as a fire that has been out for an hour rather than one still burning. The driest thing in the collection.

The oldest pairing in Arabic perfumery and the hardest to make new. The rose here is kept green and slightly sharp rather than jammy, so the oud has something to push against instead of drowning in sugar.

accords.note_to_perfumer: Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich leads, Ambroxan (10% DPG) + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Benzoin Resinoid 70 DEP (diluted 50% in BB) + Gamma Nonalactone (Aldehyde C-18) support. Immortelle smells of maple syrup and curry leaf and nothing else does. Salt keeps it from becoming a dessert, which is where it always wants to go.

accords.name: Burnt Sugar and Rum
accords.inspiration: Caramel taken one minute past ready.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Orange 10-fold Oil leads, Ethyl Maltol + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Sweetness is easy and boring. Sugar cooked until it is bitter is neither, and rum gives it the spirit edge that stops the whole thing being a pudding.

accords.name: Bitter Cocoa Dust
accords.inspiration: Cocoa before anybody has added sugar to it.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pink Pepper leads, Nutmeg EO + Coffee CO2 (10%) + Patchouli + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Cocoa absolute is bitter and dusty and smells nothing like chocolate as a sweet. Patchouli agrees with it completely; vanilla is kept well back.

accords.name: Coffee and Cardamom
accords.inspiration: The cup you are handed before anybody speaks.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom Oil RCO leads, Coffee CO2 (10%) + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Bacdanol support. Cardamom in coffee is not a flourish, it is how it is made across half the world. The perfume follows the drink rather than a dessert menu.

accords.name: Clean Linen Musk
accords.inspiration: A shirt off the line, an hour after the sun went in.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Aldehyde C-12 MNA (10%) leads, Fructone + Hedione (methyl dihydrojasmonate) + Methyl Ionone Gamma + Habanolide + Galaxolide (50%) support. The cleanest thing here, and deliberately almost nothing. Aldehyde, musk and a trace of iris — a perfume for people who do not want to smell of a perfume.

accords.name: Warm Skin Musk

accords.note_to_perfumer: Orange 10-fold Oil leads, Delta-Decalactone (wishlist) + Habanolide + Exaltolide Total support. There is a line between skin and unwashed and it is thinner than anyone admits. Cumin is here in a trace — enough to make it human, not enough to make it a problem.

accords.name: Ambrette and Cotton

accords.note_to_perfumer: Fructone leads, Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate + Methyl Ionone Gamma + Habanolide + Bacdanol support. Ambrette seed is pear skin, warm cotton and something faintly of the body, and it is the one musk that grows rather than being made. It carries the whole perfume.

accords.note_to_perfumer: Coffee CO2 (10%) leads, Patchouli support. Coffee CO2 at trace reads as pulp and ink long before it reads as coffee.

accords.name: Drying Rack
accords.inspiration: Sheets hung to dry, the whole room smelling faintly of warm paper.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) leads, Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Sweet, dusty wood — vanillin and coumarin, the classic paper-and-hay pairing.

accords.name: Fresh Ream
accords.inspiration: A stack of paper, still warm from the cutter.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Benzyl Benzoate leads, Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Clean and a little sweet, three materials that all agree with each other.

accords.name: Printer's Ink
accords.inspiration: Fresh ink on a fresh sheet, the smell of a page just off the press.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coffee CO2 (10%) leads, Guaiacol (1%) + Cypriol (Nagarmotha) support. Coffee's darkness against smoke and resin — nothing here is actually coffee.

accords.name: Binding Glue
accords.inspiration: The spine of a book, held together with warm animal glue.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Ebanol leads, Bacdanol support. Woody and faintly sweet, a small, close accord for a small, close job.

accords.name: Watermark
accords.inspiration: The mark pressed into good paper, visible only against the light.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cardamom Oil RCO leads, Coffee CO2 (10%) + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Cardamom, coffee and vanilla, all three genuinely paired with each other.

accords.name: Guillotine Trim
accords.inspiration: Off-cuts falling away as the stack is squared up.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Guaiacol (1%) leads, Labdanum Resinoid (50% in BB) + Cypriol (Nagarmotha) support. Smoke and resin, cut through with the same cypriol that runs the mill's basement.

accords.name: Archive Basement
accords.inspiration: Where the mill keeps its own back catalogue, decades deep.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coffee CO2 (10%) leads, Benzoin Resinoid 70 DEP (diluted 50% in BB) + Vanillin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) support. Coffee, benzoin and vanillin, the closest this palette gets to old paper.

accords.name: Deckle Edge
accords.inspiration: The rough, untrimmed edge of handmade paper.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) leads, Methyl Ionone Gamma + Benzoin Resinoid 70 DEP (diluted 50% in BB) support. Powdery and warm, methyl ionone gamma doing what it always does to a room.

accords.name: Warehouse Dust
accords.inspiration: The finished stock room, stacked to the ceiling.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Ebanol leads, Gamma Nonalactone (Aldehyde C-18) + Bacdanol support. Sweet, quiet wood — the last stop before a ream leaves the building.

accords.name: Bruised Sage
accords.inspiration: A leaf crushed between two fingers to test it.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clary Sage Oil leads, Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich support. Clary sage's own green-spice sharpened by bergamot underneath.

accords.name: Resin on the Cutting Board
accords.inspiration: Frankincense tears, chopped fine for a tincture.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense (Olibanum) leads, Cedarwood + Pine Essential Oil support. Woody incense propped up by pine — the whole bench smells of it after.

accords.name: Drying Bundles
accords.inspiration: Herbs hung in twine bundles from the rafters.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Lavandin Grosso leads, Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) + Linalyl Acetate support. Green and hay-like, lavandin doing most of the talking.

accords.name: Mortar and Pestle
accords.inspiration: Whatever was ground last, still clinging to the stone.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clary Sage Oil leads, Frankincense (Olibanum) + Labdanum Resinoid (50% in BB) support. Sage and frankincense meeting labdanum's warmth halfway.

accords.name: Green Glass Bottles
accords.inspiration: The apothecary's own shelf, every bottle a slightly different green.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Linalool leads, Linalyl Acetate + Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich support. Linalool and its own acetate, doubled up for volume.

accords.name: Pine Tar Ointment
accords.inspiration: An old remedy, tar and resin worked into a salve.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Pine Essential Oil leads, Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate + Geosmin (0.1% working dilution) support. Pine cut with the same petrichor pairing that runs through the whole palette.

accords.name: Weighed on Brass Scales
accords.inspiration: A dose measured out precisely, no more and no less.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Petitgrain RC leads, Vetiver EO + Frankincense (Olibanum) support. Citrus-green petitgrain against vetiver and frankincense — exact, unshowy.

accords.name: Cough Syrup, Old Recipe
accords.inspiration: A formula that hasn't changed in three generations.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Linalyl Acetate leads, Dihydromyrcenol + Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich support. Green and citrus, faintly medicinal in the way old remedies always are.

accords.name: Sun-Dried Leaves
accords.inspiration: The last tray out before the shop closes for the day.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Clary Sage Oil leads, Petitgrain RC + Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich support. Sage and petitgrain, both leaning on the same bergamot.

accords.name: The Apothecary's Coat
accords.inspiration: Worn every day for thirty years, and it shows.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Frankincense (Olibanum) leads, Bergamot INDI (reconstitution) - dsm-firmenich + Pink Pepper support. Frankincense and bergamot, warmed by a trace of pink pepper.

accords.name: Reed Bed at Low Tide
accords.inspiration: Mud exposed for a few hours until the water comes back.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Geosmin (0.1% working dilution) leads, Peatmoss (Veramoss equivalent, 10% DPG) support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Earth and moss at full strength — no citrus lift, none needed.

accords.name: Brackish Water
accords.inspiration: Where the river gives up and the sea takes over.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate leads, Geosmin (0.1% working dilution) + Floralozone support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Green rain meeting aldehydic air — fresh and stagnant in the same breath.

accords.name: Mudflat Shine
accords.inspiration: Wet mud catching the light at the water's edge.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver EO leads, Peatmoss (Veramoss equivalent, 10% DPG) + Cypriol (Nagarmotha) support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Root and resin, vetiver leaning on the same cypriol as the marsh's own peat.

accords.name: Wet Cotton on the Line
accords.inspiration: Washing that never quite dried, hung too close to the water.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Habanolide leads, Galaxolide (50%) + Dihydromyrcenol support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Musk over musk — habanolide, galaxolide and dihydromyrcenol, deliberately flat.

accords.name: Heron's Print
accords.inspiration: A single set of tracks across otherwise undisturbed mud.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Geosmin (0.1% working dilution) leads, Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Green and earthy, the marsh at its most minimal.

accords.name: Rope and Barnacle
accords.inspiration: An old mooring rope, crusted and half-buried.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Vetiver EO leads, Cedarwood + Peatmoss (Veramoss equivalent, 10% DPG) support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Wood into peat, cedar and vetiver both leaning the same direction.

accords.name: Marsh Gas at Dusk
accords.inspiration: The faint, sulphurous edge that rises as the light goes.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Geosmin (0.1% working dilution) leads, Floralozone + Cis-3-Hexenyl Acetate support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Earthy and aerated at once — the three petrichor materials at their strangest combination.

accords.name: Bleached Driftwood
accords.inspiration: Wood that's been in salt water so long it's turned grey.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Cedarwood leads, Peatmoss (Veramoss equivalent, 10% DPG) + Cypriol (Nagarmotha) support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Dry cedar meeting wet peat — two textures that shouldn't agree and do.

accords.name: Estuary Fog
accords.inspiration: Morning mist sitting low over the water.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Floralozone leads, Hedione (methyl dihydrojasmonate) support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Floral-aldehydic softness, about as gentle as this collection gets.

accords.name: Salt Grass
accords.inspiration: The tough grass that's the only thing willing to grow here.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Dihydromyrcenol leads, Floralozone support. Built wet: keep the damp/green facets forward. Aldehydic and green, aerated rather than earthy.

accords.name: Crushed Grape Skins
accords.inspiration: What's left in the press after the juice is gone.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Beta-Damascone leads, Patchouli support. Damascone's dark fruit note against patchouli's own darkness.

accords.name: Barrel Room Floor
accords.inspiration: Stained dark by decades of spillage, never quite scrubbed clean.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli leads, Rose Wardia BM support. Earthy patchouli and rose, an odd pairing that works underground.

accords.name: Late Harvest
accords.inspiration: Grapes left on the vine past the point anyone else would pick them.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Gamma Undecalactone (Aldehyde C-14) leads, Beta-Damascone support. Fruity-floral gamma undecalactone meeting damascone's own jamminess.

accords.name: Bruised Fig on the Vine
accords.inspiration: Fruit that's gone soft and dark before it's even picked.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Gamma Undecalactone (Aldehyde C-14) leads, Bacdanol support. Lactonic sweetness against sandalwood's own creaminess.

accords.name: Oak Stave
accords.inspiration: A single plank, waiting to become part of a barrel.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Coumarin (40% DPG — migrate, see spec) leads, Benzoin Resinoid 70 DEP (diluted 50% in BB) + Methyl Ionone Gamma support. Coumarin and benzoin, propped up by the same methyl ionone gamma that ages everything else here.

accords.name: First Press
accords.inspiration: The very first run of juice, before it's touched a barrel.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Rose Wardia BM leads, Beta-Damascone + Patchouli support. Rose and damascone at their brightest, patchouli held well back.

accords.name: Cellar Spider Webs
accords.inspiration: Undisturbed for a full vintage, hung with dust.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Patchouli leads, Labdanum Resinoid (50% in BB) support. Earthy patchouli anchored by labdanum's own resin.

accords.name: Ladybird on the Leaf
accords.inspiration: A single insect, the only thing moving on a still afternoon.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Gamma Undecalactone (Aldehyde C-14) leads, Jasmine Sambac support. Fruity gamma undecalactone lifted by jasmine, an orchard note wandering into the vines.

accords.name: Grape Must Fermenting
accords.inspiration: The vat two days in, already smelling of what it's becoming.
accords.note_to_perfumer: Beta-Damascone leads, Safraleine support. Rose and safraleine, spice arriving before the wine itself does.
